name: AI chips
one_line: Designs the processors that train and run AI models, then pays foundries to make them.
sells: AI accelerators (GPUs and custom chips), plus the systems and software around them
customers: Cloud companies, AI labs, big tech building its own data centers

revenue.period: derived from NVIDIA FY2026 revenue ($215.9B) / ~70% share
revenue.note: No clean public total exists. Estimated as NVIDIA's revenue divided by its ~70% share (Tom's Hardware, May 2026). Share estimates range 70–85%, and NVIDIA's revenue includes some non-AI products, so treat as a rough size.

structure.type: Dominant firm with a growing fringe
structure.why: NVIDIA sells most AI chips, but every big cloud company now designs its own custom chips, mostly with Broadcom.
structure.hhi_note: Only NVIDIA's share is sourced, so this is a lower bound.

econ: Switching costs and ecosystem lock-in: developers write software for NVIDIA's CUDA platform, which makes its chips the default even when rivals are cheaper.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.share_basis: approx. share of AI chip market (Tom's Hardware, May 2026)

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.note: Leads custom AI chips (about 70% of that segment, per Motley Fool, June 2026). Partner for Google, Meta and OpenAI chips.
products: Custom AI chips (with Google, Meta, OpenAI)

companies.name: AMD
companies.note: Second merchant GPU maker; no reliable 2026 share figure found.

companies.name: Marvell
companies.note: Custom chips for Amazon and Microsoft; projects up to $11B AI chip revenue in 2026 (Tom's Hardware).
products: Custom chips for AWS Trainium and Microsoft Maia

companies.name: Google (TPU)
companies.note: Designs its own TPUs for internal use and Google Cloud customers.

products_note: Flagship products as of Nov 2026. AI-lab and chip products checked against 2026 launch coverage; products for banks, card networks, utilities and others are long-standing lines from general knowledge, not individually cited.
